data.claim: Running the base's own test files fails the test when it pre-exists broken; else a ddflow-applied mutation of a changed test file makes it fail
data.falsifier: the new tests passing before the change, or a surviving mutation being accepted
data.mechanism: verify_regression_test overlays only the new test file on the base; a test-file fix rides along in the overlay
data.probe: tests/test_regression_testfix.py: 6 cases (restored files, mutation kills, mutation survives, mutation outside diff, CLI flags, source+test fix still refused)
data.question: Can a fix confined to test files be verified by ddflow?

evidence.note: research R-testfix-verify CONFIRMED: probe tests/test_regression_testfix.py 16 passed
ran ddflow brief --item fix-Bc262739f62; applied r-everything-configurable (test_file_globs knob + upgrade fragment, mutation params on CLI+MCP), files kept small via new modules
committed; 16 targeted tests pass, ruff check/format clean

chunk_findings.detail: If the fix deletes a test file (a legitimate test-file-only change), the loop copies that deletion into the scratch tree via `dst.unlink(missing_ok=True)`. The agent can then name that deleted file as the mutation `file` (it is in `changed`, so the `rel not in changed` guard passes, and `old` need only be non-empty), and `target.read_text("utf-8")` raises `FileNotFoundError`, crashing the close with a traceback instead of returning the intended "mutation cannot be applied" refusal (PASSES). The failure is concrete: fix deletes `tests/test_x.py`; `--mutation-file tests/test_x.py --mutation-old foo --mutation-new bar` → uncaught exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_testfix.py `_by_mutation`

chunk_findings.detail: In the "pre-fix test files restored" branch, only `outcome == "failed"` is handled; any other outcome — including `"unavailable"` (e.g. the pre-fix tree lacks a fixture/conftest introduced by the fix, so pytest cannot run there, or the gate runner is unavailable) — silently falls through to the `PASSES` branch, whose recorded reason asserts "the test also passes with the pre-fix test files restored". That records a false claim in the evidence when the run actually could not execute, conflating "could not run" with "passed". The mutation path (`_by_mutation`) treats `"unavailable"` as UNRUN precisely because it is not a pass, so the asymmetry here mis-records the verdict.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_testfix.py `verify_test_only_fix`

chunk_findings.detail: When the fix deletes a test file and the agent supplies a mutation naming that file, the copy loop takes the `else: dst.unlink(missing_ok=True)` branch, so `target` does not exist in the scratch tree. The subsequent `target.read_text("utf-8")` then raises `FileNotFoundError`, crashing the gate instead of returning a `(status, evidence)` verdict. Repro: fix deletes `tests/test_x.py` (so it appears in `changed`), and mutation is `{"file": "tests/test_x.py", "old": "...", "new": "..."}` — `rel in changed` passes, `old` is non-empty, the merge tree builds fine, and the read blows up. The same crash occurs if the fix renames the file (with `--no-renames` the old path shows up as a deletion in `changed`). The function's own contract says unapplicable mutations must be refused as PASSES, never crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_testfix.py:_by_mutation

chunk_findings.detail: `restored` is initialized to the literal string "not run (the test is not in the base's test files)", but this value is also used whenever the restored run simply never executed for another reason — specifically when `command` is empty (no gate command could be derived) the code skips `run_command_gate` entirely and `restored` keeps its initial value. In that case the refusal message claims the test "is not in the base's test files", which is false: the test may well exist in the base tree, the run just wasn't performed. This misleads the user about why verification failed and can send them down the wrong remediation path (e.g. adding the test to the base rather than fixing command discovery). Initialize with a neutral "not run" and set the specific reason only in the branch where the test file is genuinely absent from the base.
